traitor.title: Traitor's Tome
traitor.text:
### Setup
- Your explorer stays in the game and is now the traitor.
- Raise your Speed to its highest value.
- Shuffle the Medallion, which represents your Lucky Charm, into the omen stack.
- Adopt a terrible Irish accent for the rest of the game.

### Rules
#### Special Turn Order Rules
- You take a turn after each hero's turn.
#### You Must Do This on Your Turn
- If you end your turn in a room with an omen symbol [raven symbol], look at the top card of the omen stack, then put it back. Then, if you succeed at a Knowledge roll of 4+, you may shuffle the omen stack.
#### Special Attack Rules
- You cannot attack with Might except on the Rainbow.
- Anywhere else, you always make Speed attacks, rolling a number of dice equal to your Speed or to the number of room tiles on this floor that you entered before attacking, whichever is fewer. Example from the book: if you started four rooms away on this floor and your Speed is 6, you roll 4 dice; with a Speed of 3 you roll only 3 dice.
- You cannot attack anyone in the room where you started your turn (except on the Rainbow), nor can you enter a room you already left this turn.
- If you are defeated when attacking or defending, call out "Dear boy, release me!" The hero will tell you what happens then.
#### The Rainbow
- If the heroes discover the Rainbow, each Color of the Rainbow counts as 1 space of movement.
- If you stop your movement on a Color that contains a hero, or a hero ends their movement on your Color, you may immediately make a Might attack to push that hero off the Rainbow. If you succeed, the hero falls to their death.

### Traitor wins when
- All the heroes are dead.

### What they know about the other side
- The heroes are looking for your Pot of Gold, which you hid at the end of a hidden Rainbow. You don't want them to get your Lucky Charm, because then they will find the Rainbow.

> Note: The Speed-attack dice count uses "the number of room tiles on this floor that you entered before attacking", while the example counts rooms "away" from where you started; both are given as printed.

heroes.title: Secrets of Survival
heroes.text:
### Setup
- Put the pentagonal item tokens numbered 1 to 7, which represent Wishes, near the Entrance Hall.
- Set aside seven monster tokens, one of each color, which represent Colors of the Rainbow.
- Set aside a pentagonal Item Pile token, which represents the Pot of Gold.
### Rules
#### Special attack rules
- If you defeat the Leprechaun, you may pick a Wish from the Wishes table instead of dealing damage. Then put that Wish's item token back in the box. You may not pick a Wish whose item token is no longer on the table.
#### Wishes
| Wish | What Happens |
|---|---|
| 1 | Each hero draws an item card. |
| 2 | You may put your figure in any room. |
| 3 | Gain 1 Speed and 1 Might. |
| 4 | Gain 1 Sanity and 1 Knowledge. |
| 5 | Draw three events, pick one to keep, and shuffle the others into the event stack. |
| 6 | Replace any non-landing room with the top tile from the room tile stack. |
| 7 | Steal any item card or omen card from the Leprechaun, even if it can't be stolen. |
#### Special item and omen rules
- Whenever you would draw an item card, you may draw an omen card instead.
- If you draw the Medallion card, choose an open door on the roof and place the seven Colors of the Rainbow leading out from that door, in this order: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple, magenta. Then put the Pot of Gold at the end of the Rainbow.
- If there is no open door on the roof, extend the Rainbow from the side of a roof tile, treating that side as if it had a door.
#### Special movement rules
- Each Color of the Rainbow counts as its own room tile, as part of the Roof.
- At the end of any turn, only one hero may be on each Color. You may pass through a Color that contains another hero.
- If you enter the final, magenta Color, you may take the Pot of Gold and win the game. If you don't, "it's a long way down."
  > Note: "If you don't, it's a long way down" is not explained further on this page; it may imply falling off the Rainbow, or may just be flavor. The traitor's book gives no effect for it either (its only falling rule is the Leprechaun's Might push).
### Heroes win when
- You kill the Leprechaun or find the Pot of Gold.

> Note: the printed win condition is finding the Pot of Gold only, which leaves open what happens if the heroes kill the Leprechaun. The text above carries the official correction.
> Resolution (official): errata. Killing the Leprechaun also wins; the FAQ changes the win text to "you kill the Leprechaun or find the Pot of Gold". Source: https://www.dropbox.com/s/3y34f1s2tn6o4mx/Widow%27s%20Walk%20FAQ%20KB%2012.6.161.pdf?dl=0
### What they know about the other side
- The traitor has become a Leprechaun. Where there is a Leprechaun there is a Pot of Gold at the end of a Rainbow, and the heroes need to find the Rainbow.
- Leprechauns are vulnerable to being caught by their toes (the reason defeating it grants a Wish).
